materialChanges: Corrected multiplicity throughout the concept scene, subgroup examples, assessment, claim ledger, glossary, chart description, and attribution: the independence formula is exact only under independence, unknown dependence requires the joint structure, and min(1, k alpha) is the general Bonferroni upper bound.

Replaced dichotomous 'found no evidence' conclusions with quantitative estimates, confidence intervals, and the stated non-rejection decision; confined power to planning and design audit rather than treating it as completed-data evidence.
Reframed the blood-panel and physiotherapy transfer cases as conditional analogies, so neither is labelled a realised Type I or Type II error without a defined hypothesis rule and true state.
Strengthened subgroup interpretation to require a prespecified confirmatory family with multiplicity allocation and an appropriate interaction analysis for claims of heterogeneity.

Removed the unsupported use of individual fasting-glucose diagnostic categories as a yardstick for clinically meaningful between-group differences, together with the now-unused NIDDK claim and reference.
Corrected the two-sided power representation by defining beta between both critical values and disclosing the omitted, numerically negligible lower rejection tail in both prose and chart text.

Qualified long-run alpha control by the sampling or randomisation process, valid test assumptions, and a prespecified analysis rule, and added the required inverse-square self-explanation prompt to the sample-size worked example.

reviewDispositions.rationale: The multiplicity scene now states that 1-(1-alpha)^k is exact only for independent rejection events, that unspecified dependence can move the rate above or below the independent value, and that min(1,k alpha) is the general upper bound. The mapped claim, glossary definition, dependent practice check, chart description, and attribution now carry the same boundary.

The eighteen-subgroup assessment no longer demands an independence calculation: it asks learners to identify the missing dependence structure and give the valid 0.90 Bonferroni bound. Both twenty-subgroup examples now label 0.64 as an independence illustration and explicitly state that overlapping subgroup analyses require their joint dependence structure.

The non-rejection scene, faded practice, synthesis, and assessment now report the nonzero estimate, confidence interval, and failure to reject zero. A prespecified meaningful margin plus an interval or direct equivalence test supplies evidence for bounded absence; power is retained only as a planning or design-audit quantity.

The transfer scene now says the pilot creates a Type II error risk only if a true benefit exists and reports its estimate and interval. It also states that an out-of-range value in a healthy individual is not a Type I error without a formal null, decision rule, and true state; the revised check assesses those conditional distinctions.

Prespecification is no longer presented as sufficient. The lesson, claim ledger, glossary, assessment feedback, reference use record, and source notes now require multiplicity allocation within a prespecified confirmatory strategy and an appropriate treatment-by-subgroup interaction analysis for claims that effects differ.

The diagnostic-band comparison and unsupported usefulness judgement were removed from the synthesis. The now-unused NIDDK health-sensitive claim and reference were removed from claims.json, references.json, the learner-visible source note, and ATTRIBUTION.md.

The chart and coordinated prose now define two-sided power as both rejection tails and beta as the alternative-curve area between -8.09 and +8.09. They explicitly state that the rendered shading omits the lower power component of about 0.00002 because it is numerically negligible and does not change the rounded result.

The alpha discussion now conditions the long-run rate on a valid sampling or randomisation process, valid test assumptions, and an analysis rule fixed before seeing results. The multiplicity scene repeats the valid-test and prespecification boundary.

The 80%-power sample-size worked example now asks learners to self-explain why reducing the target difference increases required sample size with the inverse square, and it points them through the proportional-standard-error and inverse-square sample-size links.
This is a positive first-read note with no requested resolution. The concrete opening, motivating questions, diagnostic check, and recovery route were preserved unchanged.

This is a positive representation note with no requested resolution. The dual-curve representation and prose coordination were retained; the separate academic finding was incorporated by correcting the two-sided tail and beta description without removing the representation.

This is a positive practice-and-transfer note with no requested resolution. The varied practice and novel blood-panel and physiotherapy contexts remain; only their error classifications and completed-data interpretation were corrected for academic accuracy.

evidenceChecked: All eight scene files retain exactly one level-one heading, logical source order, text-first prompts and feedback, and no raw HTML tags or entities.

Both local declarative charts retain concise alt text, outcome-equivalent long descriptions, numerical data, labelled axes and markers, and explanations that do not rely on colour, position, hover, motion, or visual estimation.

All checks and assessment items can be completed from printed text and mathematics without pointer, drag, audio, timing, personal health data, or remote interaction; the recovery route and teaching-example boundary remain learner-visible.

Every retained claim resolves to a retained source and appears in each mapped scene's learner-visible source note with all supporting source IDs; all five sources record factual-reference use, facts-only original expression, dated agent-access checks, and no human-only restriction.

The pack declares CC BY 4.0, identifies the accountable principal and author-agent provenance, lists no third-party assets, and ATTRIBUTION.md identifies the charts, cases, calculations, prompts, and prose as original material.

The lesson contains no remote embed, executable content, unsafe TeX command, SVG, secret, identifiable learner or patient data, or clinical instruction; all cases are fictional and the revised transfer explicitly defers clinical follow-up decisions to applicable guidance.
limitations: This was a static source audit; no rendered browser, 200% zoom/reflow, keyboard-only, screen-reader, reduced-motion, print, or non-web export test was available in this run.

The finalizer audited the recorded source-access, licence, and original-expression ledgers but did not independently refetch every source or obtain legal advice; rights provenance remains an accountable attestation rather than a legal guarantee.

Per the operator's instruction, npm source preflight and repository validation were not run. Pack-local JSON parsing, cross-reference checks, string/date/length checks, raw-HTML and unsafe-content scans, and git diff whitespace checks passed.

rationale: The supplied record contains exactly two eligible advisory inputs against the original candidate: one academic and one learning-design review, both with request-changes verdicts, distinct run IDs, and two declared provider/model families. Their equivalent GitHub transports were supplied as non-dismissed COMMENTED reviews; this run did not independently query GitHub. The shared accountable principal and the learning-design review's declared conflict are permitted by the founding-stage policy but are preserved as a limitation, not represented as verified independence. All eight academic findings and the one actionable learning-design finding were incorporated; the remaining three learning-design findings were positive notes requiring no separate change. The final content now uses dependence-valid multiplicity logic, quantitative interval-based reporting of non-rejections, conditional error classifications, a confirmatory subgroup boundary, an accurate two-sided power representation, and a narrower health-sensitive scope. Pack-local structural, mapping, rights, accessibility-source, security, and whitespace checks passed, and the final static accessibility-and-rights audit found no unresolved blocker. A merge decision is therefore supported, subject to the operator replacing the pending final-commit placeholder with the exact committed content SHA and obtaining the required repository validation and GitHub-provenance checks before merge.
dissent: Both eligible advisory reviews returned request-changes rather than approval. Their actionable concerns are incorporated here, but neither reviewer is represented as having reviewed or approved the final revision.

The learning-design reviewer declared that github:VSBDev operates authoring, review, and finalization runs. The policy permits one founding-stage principal, but principal-level independence is absent and agent provenance is disclosed and attested rather than externally verified.

No real learner testing, assistive-technology session, rendered export inspection, or empirical model validation was available; the learning and accessibility judgments remain evidence-based static review.
conditions: Before adjudication submission or merge, the accountable operator must commit the final lesson content with both cited review artifacts, replace PENDING-FINAL-COMMIT with that exact 40-character SHA, and make no further teaching-content change.
The operator must run the required strict source preflight and repository validation and proceed only if all pack schemas, governance invariants, and GitHub transport/provenance checks pass.
After the real finalCommit is recorded, the maintainer may make only the separately permitted publication transition to lesson status, source confidence, and retained claim review-status fields.
